Foundations / Color

Foundations

Color

The Halo UI palette, semantic color roles, and the contrast rules every product must follow.

stable

Color in Halo UI is expressed in two layers. The base palette is a fixed set of perceptually-even ramps. Semantic roles map those ramps to meaning — surface, text, border, brand, danger — so a product never references a raw hex value directly.

Brand ramp

Indigo is the Lumen Labs brand color. The 600 step is the default interactive fill; 700 is its hover state; 100 is the soft background used by soft variants.

Status ramps

Status colors are never used decoratively. Reserve them for the meaning they encode: success, caution, and error.

Neutrals

The neutral ramp carries text, surfaces, and borders. It is very slightly cool-tinted (a touch of indigo) so it never reads as muddy beside the brand.

Semantic roles

Components consume roles, not ramp steps. This indirection is what lets a single theme swap recolor the whole system.

RoleLight themeDark theme
--halo-surfaceslate/0slate/900
--halo-surface-raisedslate/0#14172a
--halo-textslate/900slate/100
--halo-text-mutedslate/500slate/300
--halo-borderslate/100#262a40
--halo-brandindigo/600indigo/500
--halo-dangerrose/700rose/500

Never hard-code hex

If you find yourself writing color: #4f46e5 in a product, that's a bug. Use var(--halo-brand). Hard-coded values break theming and silently fail the high-contrast theme audit.

Contrast requirements

Every text/background pairing in a Halo UI product must meet WCAG 2.2 AA: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text (≥ 24px, or 19px bold) and for the focus ring against adjacent colors. The token build runs a contrast check on every semantic pairing and fails CI if a combination drops below threshold.

Do

Pair --halo-text on --halo-surface (16.1:1) for body copy.

Don't

Put slate/500 text on a slate/100 background — that's only 3.0:1 and fails AA for body text.

Note

Want the full numeric matrix? Run pnpm tokens:build and open tokens/report/contrast.html — it grades all 612 role pairings.
